### Added
- **The stateful singletons can be pinned to on-demand capacity, and muster-valkey takes the #431 guards** (giantswarm/agent-platform#439; on gazelle, all-spot workers, one spot-interruption wave took muster's OAuth token store down for two minutes — every token refresh blocked inside muster, 27 s before the Slack bot reacted — and killed klaus-gateway mid-turn, its replacement waiting four minutes on `Multi-Attach`). #431's guards address *voluntary* disruption only; a spot reclaim terminates the instance whatever the budget says. New meta-chart block **`scheduling.singletons`** (`nodeSelector`, `tolerations`; **empty by default, so no installation changes behaviour until it is set**): merged into, and appended to, the scheduling knobs of the four single-replica stateful pods before their releases render — muster (`muster.nodeSelector`), muster-valkey (`valkey.valkey.nodeSelector`), the kagent controller (`kagent.controller.nodeSelector`), klaus-gateway (`klausGateway.nodeSelector`) — with a component's own keys winning (`agent-platform.scheduling.apply`); held back from the connectivity release (`components.agent-platform-connectivity.omitKeys`), so a live connectivity chart that predates the block is never failed by it. The intended value on a Karpenter spot installation is `karpenter.sh/capacity-type: on-demand` (one small on-demand node for the four; the fleet's NodePools admit it untainted) — UPGRADE.md carries the cost note, the roll and the "never on a cluster without Karpenter" warning. klaus-gateway takes the keys from chart 1.3.3 on (giantswarm/klaus-gateway#253: the earlier 1.x schemas refused every key under `nodeSelector` — found in the lab when the release failed validation). **muster-valkey** now carries `karpenter.sh/do-not-disrupt: "true"` (the valkey subchart's `valkey.valkey.podAnnotations`) and a `PodDisruptionBudget muster-valkey` (`valkey.podDisruptionBudget`, `minAvailable: 1`, `AlwaysAllow`) rendered by the connectivity chart — neither the wrapper nor the upstream subchart has a budget knob — selecting the pod as the subchart labels it (name `valkey`, instance `valkey`), named after `valkey.valkey.fullnameOverride`; the key never reaches the valkey release (`components.valkey.omitKeys`). Every installation rolls the `muster-valkey` pod once. `make verify-disruption` extended: the merge and its precedence, the empty default (byte-identical component values), the hold-back, the valkey budget on/off/inert and its guards, a stray key under the block refused by the schema.
